photo_details.label: ACTUAL REPRODUCTIVE MACRO · scaled intact spikelets
photo_details.role: Multiple exact-species attached green spikelets beside original millimeter scale; some veins visible but not verified glume-number
photo_details.caption: Bob Harms' Central Texas Reverchon's bristlegrass photograph shows multiple genuine green/purple spikelets branching beside an original physical millimeter ruler. A bristle is a reduced inflorescence branch, not an awn. Do not infer glume vein counts or identify a tiny hairy ligule here.

photo_details.label: TRUE AXIS DETAIL · reproductive disarticulation
photo_details.role: Authentic flowering axis, several spaced purple mottled spikelets and separation points, with original millimeter reference
photo_details.caption: Actual photographed Reverchon's bristlegrass mature spikelets are separated along the thin branched rachis rather than packed into one continuous dense foxtail. Source image includes a ruler; the complete microscopic internal glume/lemma dissection is not pictured.
